1  Date : 16/02/2017  ORAL JUDGMENT HC-NIC Page 1 of 4 Created On Sun Aug 13 16:42:56 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/54/2016 JUDGMENT 1. By way of present Criminal Revision Application preferred under Section 397 read with Section 401 of the Code of the Criminal Procedure, the applicant - State seeks to challenge the order passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Pardi, in Criminal Case No.462 of 2007 dated 30.7.2014, whereby the learned trial Judge acquitted the respondents - accused for the offences under Sections 2(ia), (a), 2(ia), (j), 7(i), 7(iii), 7(v), 16(1) (A) (1) and 16(1) (A) (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

2. As per the case of the prosecution, on 9.10.2006, at about 15:15 Hrs. the complainant along with witness Arvindbhai Manibhai Patel visited the place of the accused and at that time, the accused was doing his business.
The complainant as Food Inspector, asked for certificate running "Ahar Gruh".
The same was produced.
Thereafter, the complainant asked for other licence, if the accused is having, and the accused answered that he is not having such licence.
On inspection of the hotel, in one big utensil, some foodstuff was stored and same was loose "Alumutar" prepared food an was to be served to the customer, as per the accused.

Therefore, the complainant was having doubt about colouring agent being added, sample of the said foodstuff was taken and necessary proceedings in that regard was carried out including sending of the sample for analysis.
The public analyst reported about colouring agents and hence, the sample was found to be adulterated as per the provisions of the Act.
Thereafter, necessary documents were collected and permission was sought for prosecuting the accused and same was granted.
The trial was conducted and the accused were acquitted for the charges levelled against them.
Therefore, present Criminal Revision Application is filed by the applicant State.
HC-NIC Page 2 of 4 Created On Sun Aug 13 16:42:
R/CR.RA/54/2016 JUDGMENT 3.

Learned APP Mr. N.J.Shah appearing for the applicant - State submitted that there is prima facie evidence against the applicant and the provisions of Rule 29 which is directly attracted to the case of the accused.

He also submitted that the public analyst report reflects the adulteration and therefore,
it can be said that the accused committed alleged offence.
He also submitted that the accused was not having even the licence for running "Ahar Gruh."

He further submitted that the prosecution has established the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt and therefore, the impugned order is required to be quashed and set aside and accused may be convicted and sentenced for the State Of Gujarat vs Bhaveshkumar Dahyabhai Rabari & on 16 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53635175/
2 alleged offences.

sentences.text: 4. As against, learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 has strongly opposed the application and supported the impugned order passed by the trial Court.
He also submitted that the public analyst report Exhibit 73 as per the public analyst, is to be superseded in the case of loose prepared food.
In these circumstances, learned advocate prayed to dismiss the present application by confirming the order of the trial Court.
5. Perused the application along with its relevant record and considered the submissions made by the learned advocate for the parties.

It appears that the licence for running "Ahar Gruh"
was not on the day of incident, is not believable because the accused had already written letter for its renewal.
It is also appears that the prosecution has not followed mandatory provisions as prescribed under the Act.
Even the report HC-NIC Page 3 of 4 Created On Sun Aug 13 16:42:56 IST 2017 R/CR.RA/54/2016 JUDGMENT produced at Exhibit 73 can be said as null and void as per the provisions of the Act.
Therefore, the learned trial Judge has rightly acquitted the accused for the charges levelled against the accused.
Hence, this Court has no reason to interfere with the impugned order passed by the trial Court.
In view of the above, present Criminal Revision Application is rejected.
Rule is discharged.

(Z.K.SAIYED, J.) YNVYAS HC-NIC Page 4 of 4 Created On Sun Aug 13 16:42:56 IST 2017 State Of Gujarat vs Bhaveshkumar Dahyabhai Rabari & on 16 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53635175/
